about: Hand-checked key human results. Each entry overrides the automatic keyword verdict for the same study and counts toward its one mechanism only (the treatment's own mechanism). Read by msac/analysis.py; grading rules are in analysis.MechanismScore.grade.

fields.ids: Every identifier of the same study (PMID as pmid:N, DOI as doi:..., ClinicalTrials.gov NCT number, or URL). The first is the study's key.
fields.label: Short name used in the grade's Why line.
fields.design: randomized and placebo (true/false), phase, n (participants), n_source (where n comes from).
fields.endpoints: umsars and imaging: improved | no_benefit | null (null = not recorded here).
fields.note: One line, shown on the mechanism page.

results.label: ATH434-201
results.title: ATH434-201: ATH434 in multiple system atrophy (Phase 2)
results.note: 50 mg showed a significant benefit on UMSARS part I; 75 mg did not.

results.label: ATH434-202
results.title: ATH434-202: open-label ATH434 study in multiple system atrophy (Phase 2)
results.note: Open-label Phase 2; the company reported the results as positive.

results.label: Lee 2012, Annals of Neurology
results.title: A randomized trial of mesenchymal stem cells in multiple system atrophy.
results.note: Mesenchymal stem cells slowed UMSARS worsening compared with placebo in people with MSA-C.

results.label: PROMESA (EGCG)
results.title: Safety and efficacy of epigallocatechin gallate in multiple system atrophy (PROMESA).
results.note: EGCG did not slow UMSARS worsening compared with placebo. Counted for α-synuclein aggregation only.
